       ​I.INTRODUCTION​​AND​​STATEMENT​​OF​​THE​​CASE​

I​ntervenor​ ​Bruce​​Edward​​Burnett​​is​​the​​owner​​of​​approximately​​104​​acres​​of​​land​
 ​located​​in​​Bell​​County,​​Texas.​​Proposed​​Route​​Segment/Link​​A2​​as​​filed​​by​​the​
  ​Applicants​​LCRA​​Transmission​​Services​​Corporation​​(LCRA​​TSC)​​and​​Oncor​​Electric​
   ​Delivery​​Company​​LLC​​(Oncor)​​crosses​​Intervenor’s​​property​​for​​approximately​​2,100​
    ​linear​​feet,​​traversing​​improved​​pastures,​​native​​type​​rangeland​​,​​cultivated​​land​
     ​(interseeded,​​drilled​​forage)​​creek​​bottom​​(Glass​​Branch)​​all​​of​​which​​is​​either​
      ​temporarily​​or​​permanently​​cross-fenced​​within​​substantial​​boundary​​fencing​​of​​our​
       ​property.​

I​ntervenor​​timely​​intervened​​in​​this​​proceeding​​and​​submitted​​direct​​testimony​​filed​​on​
 ​the​​PUC​​Interchange​​at​​Item​​Number​​5474.​ ​The​​Hearing​​on​​Merits​​was​​conducted​
  ​June​​8​​through​​12,2026.​ ​This​​Brief​​is​​submitted​​pursuant​​to​​the​​SOAH​​Order​​governing​

 ​evidence​​in​​the​​record.​ ​Exhibit​​and​​transcript​​citations​​should​​be​​inserted​​at​​the​
  ​bracketed​​references.​
      ​1.​ ​Intervenor​​Bruce​​Edward​​Burnett​​owns​​approximately​​104​​acres​​located​​on​​tracts​
                ​3502​​and​​3503​​as​​identified​​by​​the​​Applicants​​in​​Bell​​County,​​Texas.​​[Cite:​
                 ​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony.]​
       ​2.​ ​Proposed​​Route​​Segment/Link​​A2​​would​​cross​​Intervenor’s​​property​​for​
                  ​approximately​​2,100​​linear​​feet,​​entering​​at​​the​​front​​of​​Intervenor’s​​property​​on​
                   ​U.S.​​Highway​​190​​and​​diagonally​​bisecting​​the​​Intervenor’s​​tracts​​3502​​and​​3503​
                    ​and​​exiting​​Intervenor’s​​property​​on​​the​​West​​side​​of​​the​​Intervenor’s​​tracts​​of​
                     ​land.This​​would​​fragment​​our​​two​​largest​​pastures​​creating​​untold​​operational​
                      ​difficulties.​​[Cite:Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Applicant’s​​Direct​​Testimony​​via​
                       ​CCN​​Application.]​
        ​3.​ ​The​​proposed​​crossing​​would​​bisect​​Intervenor’s​​improved​​pasture,​​native​
                        ​pasture,​​Creek​​bottomland​​(Glass​​Branch)​​rendering​​approximately​​104​​acres​
                         ​difficult​​or​​impossible​​to​​access​​and​​use​​as​​intended.[Cite:​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​
                          ​Testimony.]​
         ​4.​ ​The​​proposed​​route​​crosses​​within​​a​​close​​distance​​of​​our​​dry​​cabin​​and​​our​
                           ​cattle​​working​​pens​​(corral).​​[Cite:Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony.]​

                            ​community​​and​​on​​Txdot​​maps.​​[Cite:Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony.]​

                            ​III.​​PROPOSED​​CONCLUSIONS​​OF​​LAW​

   ​1.​ ​The​​PUC​​has​​jurisdiction​​over​​this​​proceeding​​pursuant​​to​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​
             ​Sections​​37.051​​and​​37.056.​
    ​2.​ ​The​​applicable​​standard​​for​​approval​​of​​a​​CCN​​for​​a​​new​​transmission​​line​​is​
              ​governed​​by​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​​37.056(c),​​which​​directs​​the​
               ​Commission​​to​​consider:​​(a)​​the​​adverse​​effects​​on​​the​​scenic,aesthetic,​​and​
                ​recreational​​value​​of​​the​​surrounding​​area;​​(b)​​the​​effects​​on​​the​​natural​
                 ​environment​​,​​historic​​sites​​and​​areas​​of​​particular​​environmental​​concern;​​(c)​​the​
                  ​effects​​on​​vegetation,water,fish​​and​​wildlife;​​(d)​​whether​​the​​route​​utilizes​​existing​
                   ​compatible​​rights-of-way;​​(e)​​the​​effects​​on​​residential​​and​​commercial​
                    ​development;​​(f)​​whether​​the​​route​​conforms​​with​​the​​policy​​of​​prudent​
                     ​avoidance;​​and​​(g)​​community​​values,recreational​​and​​park​​areas,​​historical​​and​
                      ​aesthetic​​values,​​environmental​​integrity​​and​​the​​probable​​improvement​​of​
                       ​service​​or​​lowering​​of​​cost​​to​​consumers​​in​​the​​area.​
     ​3.​ ​The​​Commission​​is​​not​​required​​to​​approve​​any​​particular​​route​​segment/link​
                        ​proposed​​by​ ​the​​Applicants.​​All​​122​​alternative​​routes​​and​​route​​links​​included​​in​
                         ​the​​CCN​​Application​​are​​available​​for​​selection​​and​​approval​​by​​the​​PUC.​​See​
                          ​CCN​​Application​​(March​​26,​​2026).​
      ​4.​ ​The​​evidence​​in​​this​​record​​does​​not​​support​​approval​​of​​Route​​Segment/Link​​A2​
                           ​as​​the​​preferred​​routing​​across​​Intervenor’s​​Property​​(tract​​3502,3503)​​because​
                            ​the​​proposed​​765kv​​transmission​​line​​would​​be​​close​​to​​our​​working​​pens​​(steel​
                             ​construction)​​and​​our​​dry​​cabin​​as​​well​​as​​our​​creek​​(Glass​​Branch)​​creating​
                              ​problems​​for​​our​​operation.​ ​The​​segment​​would​​diagonally​​cross​​our​​property​​for​
                               ​approximately​​2,100​​linear​​feet​​bisecting​​our​​two​​largest​​pastures​​(and​​fields​​we​
                                ​plant​​forage​​in​​)making​​it​​difficult​​if​​not​​impossible​​to​​access​​and​​utilize​​for​​the​
                                 ​best​​outcome​​in​​our​​ranching​​operation.​
       ​5.​ ​An​​alternative​​route/link​​or​​combination​​of​​route​​segments/links​​is​​available​​in​​the​
                                  ​record​​that​​better​​satisfies​​the​​factors​​set​​forth​​in​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​
                                   ​37.056(c)​​as​​applied​​to​​the​​corridor​​traversing​​Intervenor”s​​property.​

       ​IV.ARGUMENT​

​ .THE​​STATUTORY​​FACTORS​​WEIGH​​AGAINST​​SELECTION​​OF​​ROUTE​​A2​
A
​ACROSS​​INTERVENOR’S​​PROPERTY.​
      ​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​​37.056(c)​​sets​​forth​​the​​factors​​the​​Commission​
       ​must​​weigh​​in​​selecting​​a​​CCN​​route.​ ​The​​evidence​​introduced​​at​​the​​Hearing​​on​
        ​the​​Merits​​demonstrates​​that​​several​​of​​these​​factors​​weigh​​against​​the​​selection​
         ​of​​Segment/Link​​A2​​as​​the​​route​​crossing​​Intervenor’s​​property.​

   ​1.​ ​COMMUNITY​​VALUES,​​AESTHETIC​​VALUES​​AND​​EFFECTS​​ON​
         ​RESIDENTIAL​​DEVELOPMENT.​
          ​Segment/Link​​A2​​would​​place​​765kv​​transmission​​towers​​within​​our​​property​
           ​boundaries​​for​​approximately​​2,100​​linear​​feet​​diagonally​​bisecting​​our​​two​
            ​largest​​pastures​​of​​our​​ranch​​fundamentally​​fragmenting​​the​​character​​of​​our​
             ​rural​​ranchland.​ ​Our​​family​​has​​occupied​​this​​property​​since​​1955​​stewarding​
              ​this​​property​​and​​making​​improvements​​all​​along​​the​​way.​ ​Our​​family​​has​
               ​ranched​​this​​property​​for​​over​​seventy​​years.​

       ​ nlike​​conventional​​distribution​​structures,765kv​​towers​​are​​among​​the​​tallest​
       U
       ​transmission​​structures​​proposed​​for​​construction​​anywhere​​in​​Texas,​​standing​
        ​approximately​​185​​feet​​in​​height.​ ​Their​​proximity​​to​​our​​ranches​​interior​
         ​implicates​​both​​community​​values​​and​​the​​prudent​​avoidance​​policy​​recognized​
          ​in​​Section​​37.056(c).​​See​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony.​

   ​2.​ ​AVAILABILITY​​OF​​EXISTING​​OR​​COMPATIBLE​​RIGHTS-of-WAY.​
         ​Alternative​​Segment/Link​​A3​​is​​in​​close​​proximity​​to​​existing​​industrial​​operations​
          ​that​​include​​solar​​farms,​​battery​​electric​​storage​​facilities,​​large​​transmission​​lines​
           ​as​​well​​as​​large​​electrical​​substations.​ ​Our​​property​​(tracts​​3502​​and​​3503)​​is​
            ​unencumbered​​at​​this​​time​​from​​any​​transmission​​line​​rights-of-way​​as​​well​​as​
             ​any​​other​​industrial​​type​​equipment.​ ​See​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony​​and​
              ​Applicants​​Appendix​​C,​​page​​C-47-Figure​​6-29​​Revision​​of​​Link​​A3​​in​​the​​EA.​

       I.INTRODUCTION AND STATEMENT OF THE CASE

Intervenor Bruce Edward Burnett is the owner of approximately 104 acres of land
located in Bell County Texas. Proposed Route Segment/Link A2 as filed by the
Applicants LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (LCRA TSC) and Oncor Electric
Delivery Company LLC (Oncor) crosses Intervenor's property for approximately 2,100
linear feet, traversing improved pastures, native type rangeland, cultivated land
(interseeded, drilled forage) creek bottom (Glass Branch) all of which is either
temporarily or permanently cross-fenced within substantial boundary fencing of our
property.

Intervenor timely intervened in this proceeding and submitted direct testimony filed on
the PUC Interchange at Item Number 5474. The Hearing on Merits was conducted
June 8 through 12,2026. This Brief is submitted pursuant to the SOAH Order governing

post-hearing Briefing and is filed in accordance with the June 19,2026 deadline
established by the Administrative Law Judge.

Intervenor respectfully urges the Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) to recommend to the
Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC or Commission) that the proposed route
segmenUIink crossing or adjacent to Intervenor's property not be selected, and that the
Commission instead approve an alternative route or combination of route
segments/links that avoids the Intervenor's property or materially reduces adverse
impacts upon it.

                     Il.PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT

Intervenor proposes the following findings of fact, each of which is supported by
evidence in the record. Exhibit and transcript citations should be inserted at the
bracketed references.
   1. Intervenor Bruce Edward Burnett owns approximately 104 acres located on tracts
      3502 and 3503 as identified by the Applicants in Bell County, Texas. [Cite:
      Intervenor's Direct Testimony.]
   2. Proposed Route SegmenULink A2 would cross Intervenor's property for
      approximately 2,100 linear feet, entering at the front of Intervenor's property on
      U.S. Highway 190 and diagonally bisecting the Intervenor's tracts 3502 and 3503
      and exiting Intervenor's property on the West side of the Intervenor's tracts of
      land.This would fragment our two largest pastures creating untold operational
      difficulties. [Cite:Intervenor's Direct Testimony; Applicant's Direct Testimony via
      CCN Application.]
